newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson says planned well for inventories.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson says planned well for inventories.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp, a huge retailer that includes Target, Mervyn's and Marshall Field's department stores, said on Tuesday it was accurate in stocking its shelves with merchandise.
"We planned very well for inventory and we are basically on plan," said Gail Dorn, a spokeswoman for Minneapolis-based Dayton Hudson.
While specific results were not available, Dorn said, "anecdotically, sales were brisk and there were moderate crowds today."

Sales of electronics, home furnishings, particularly picture frames and candles as well as bath items were strong, she said. Clothing overall is doing well, especially sales of intimate apparel and men's furnishings.
Geographically, California is showing some improvement over last year as a region, she told Reuters.

Dayton Hudson's Target division, which operates 736 stores, showed strong sales in Texas, Chicago and Arizona. Sales were brisk in electronics, home furnishings, sporting goods, especially bicycle sales, watches and fragrances.
In its Mervyn's division, which includes 300 stores, sales of accessories, intimate apparel and menswear were strong.
And in its department store division, which includes 68 stores, sales of better sportswear, intimate apparel and menswear showed gains.
In mid-November, Dayton Hudson chairman Bob Ulrich had said the retailer was well positioned for a successful finish to 1996, despite five fewer shopping days to the holiday shopping season.
Shares of Dayton Hudson, which operates a total of 1,104 stores, closed off 1/4 to 38-3/4.
